newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico banking leader says rates could fall more.
newsitem.headline: Mexico banking leader says rates could fall more.

text.p: Mexican interest rates may continue to fall and even reach 1994 levels, said Pedro Zorrilla Velasco, chairman of the Mexican Bankers' Association.
"I think that (interest rates) will at least be at the levels we have right now, without ruling out further falls, and we may reach similar levels to the end of 1994," Zorrilla said.
"The expectation is that ... if the inflationary outlook comes down, as it has been, rates will keep falling further," he added.
"A tight monetary policy is spoken of as a necessary evil. I would say monetary discipline has allowed interest rates to come down faster than a lax policy," Zorrilla said.
